Green Card vs Residence Permit: The Difference Sellers Blur

The two terms are used interchangeably in Telegram adverts and they are not the same tier. Getting this wrong is the difference between permanent status and a two year card.

Outside the United States almost nobody issues a green card, because the green card is an American artefact. Sellers use the phrase anyway because it searches well, and that is where the confusion starts.

A green card is the United States permanent resident card, form I-551. It grants the right to live and work in the United States indefinitely and it is renewable rather than re-applied for. The register behind it is the USCIS alien registration system.

A residence permit is the fixed term card a country issues to a foreign national it has allowed to stay. It carries a class, a purpose and an expiry date, and renewal depends on the conditions still being met. Almost every country in the world has this tier.

The difference is not cosmetic. A permanent card survives a change of job, a change of address and a change of marital status. A fixed term permit can lapse on any of them, and the register entry is what determines whether it does.

Price reflects the difference. Permanent cards sit at three hundred and fifty to sixteen hundred dollars in observed adverts, because the number has to sit in an immigration register. Fixed term permits sit below that, usually three hundred to fourteen hundred.

When a seller advertises a green card for France or Germany, ask which register the number sits in. If the answer is a national immigration register, the card is a permanent residence card and the word green card is being used loosely. If the answer is vague, the seller is repeating your words.

The tell on the card itself is the class code. Permanent cards carry a class that means permanent, and it is printed in a field you can read. Fixed term permits carry a class tied to a purpose, such as work, study or family, and it usually expires with the card.

Check the expiry relationship too. A permanent card normally runs five or ten years. A fixed term permit runs for the length of the underlying permission, often one or two years. A card labelled permanent with a two year expiry is a contradiction worth asking about.

Quick answers

Finally, ask what happens at renewal. A permanent card is renewed on payment. A fixed term permit is renewed on evidence. Sellers who cannot describe the renewal step are selling the look of the card and nothing behind it.

Is a residence permit worth buying?

Only if the class matches what you actually need. A permit that authorises study is useless to somebody who needs to work.

Why do adverts say green card for every country?

Because it is the term buyers search for. It is marketing language, not a document category.
